chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Nuflī, from al-Sakkūnī, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him), that a man came to him and said to him:
I have vowed to slaughter my son at the Station of Abraham, if I do such and such. So I did it. Ali (peace be upon him) said: Slaughter a fat sheep, and give its meat in charity to the poor.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a vow to slaughter a person?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling for a man who vowed to slaughter his son, demonstrating the principle of *kaffarah* (expiation) through animal sacrifice rather than literal human sacrifice. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that vows involving specific actions are binding but can be redeemed with equivalent sacrifices, preserving the dignity of the individual. The narrative underscores the practical application of vow fulfillment in early Islamic jurisprudence, emphasizing charity and accessibility over extreme measures.
